about: How a lesson is built (unit-prep design section 6.2). Numbers are working numbers; basis names where each one comes from.

skeleton.rule: One card per new lemma the card places here, in the card's order. Each new word is first met in a sentence made of known words; a word taught earlier gets a review row, never a second card.
One concept card per construction, with a French example built from words the learner already knows.

A verb whose forms the lesson teaches gets a conjugation that names the verb: {"verb": "vouloir", "en": "to want"}, with aspect progressive when the English is I'm leaving, gloss when the English verb is not the en (can for pouvoir), and note for a line of the lesson's own on the sound map. The forms, sound groups, stems, silent letters, the model verb and what to listen for between il and ils are built from the graph. L's Verb forms step teaches each form from it: the sound map, each form met and said, each form typed from memory and checked off only when right, il and ils heard side by side, then who is it by ear. The forms need no cards; the infinitive keeps its card. Every person needs a sentence among the items, a gapfill with a gloss or a respond item with a cue, with vous and ils or elles each in at least one: every form comes back in review inside one of them. No item asks a form on its own (je veux): ask it in a sentence with the form as the blank.
A table only for a set of forms that is not one verb's present (a contraction set, possessives). A verb's forms go in the conjugation, never a bare table.
Pronunciation phrases include at least one word with the card's sound focus.
Open and close with items set in a card situation.

accept.rule: When the situation does not say who is spoken to, accept both {tu} and {vous}.
When the situation does not fix the question form, accept intonation, {est-ce que} and inversion.
When the speaker's gender is not fixed, accept both agreements.
Accept both apostrophes and spacing variants; the answer checker already does.

drafter_rules: The card's words are this lesson's only new cards.
If the lesson needs another new word, a small grammar word included, name it in drafter_notes or return cannot_satisfy with word_untaught.
A word taught earlier never gets a second card; to show it again, use a review row.
Names, cognates and sound words may appear without a card.
Introduce each new word in a sentence made of words the learner already knows, so its meaning comes from what they own.
Teach the words the card lists first before the words that build on them, in the card's order.
At least a fifth of the exercises use a word new in this lesson to carry the next new word, so each new word is used again before the lesson ends.
A different form of a word already taught gets a gloss row, never a card, with the fields fr, en and note.
A gloss row's fr is the form exactly as the text spells it, en gives its meaning, and note names the form: for {volerait}, "would fly (conditional of {voler})".
A gloss row's fr never repeats the fr of a vocabulary card in the same module.
